site.title: Working Together
site.intro: Photography about people, space and presence.
site.description: I am not interested in producing an idealised version of a person. I look for photographs in which gesture, light, distance, surroundings and the moments between actions become part of the image.

expect.title: The photograph is more than its subject.
expect.intro: A successful session is not measured by how many different looks we produce. The aim is a coherent body of photographs with character — images that can remain direct, quiet, ambiguous or open, depending on what the work needs.

items.title: Not perfection
items.text: Beauty can be present, but it is not the objective. Character, honesty and ambiguity are often more interesting than an idealised image.

items.title: The whole frame matters
items.text: The person does not always have to dominate the photograph. Space, light, objects, shadows and other people can carry equal weight.

items.title: Moments over poses
items.text: Some photographs are directed. Others appear while moving, waiting, speaking, turning away or simply doing nothing for a moment.

items.title: A connected result
items.text: I am interested in photographs that belong together. The result may move between portrait, observation and context while remaining one visual language.

series.caption: A person can be the centre of the image — or one element inside a larger situation.

process.title: Construct the situation. Then observe.
paragraphs: I work from the position of an observer, even when a portrait session is carefully planned. Light, space, clothing or a location may be deliberately constructed, but once the situation exists I prefer to watch what develops inside it rather than constantly interfere with it.

I do not photograph continuously and I do not need to replace one pose with the next. I often stay with a position, a light or a space, give it time and look for the point at which gesture, expression, distance and surroundings come together.
This requires concentration from both sides. Mutual trust, clear communication and respect for personal boundaries are simply part of that process.
process.quote: I am less interested in producing many different photographs than in finding the strongest photograph within a situation.

series.caption: Small changes can alter the meaning of an image more than a completely new setup.

work.title: Two different starting points.
work.intro: You either commission me for a defined photographic purpose, or we meet because a free project connects with both of us. The distinction is simple and helps us keep expectations clear.

workingFormats.lead: You need photographs for a defined purpose. We agree on what they need to communicate before we begin.
workingFormats.description: A commission can result in a clear and direct portrait, an editorial series, campaign imagery or quieter photographs in which the person becomes part of a larger space or situation. The purpose guides the work, while the photographic language remains recognisably mine.

series.caption: The result is defined by purpose, not by a fixed formula.

details.title: Purpose
details.text: We start with where the photographs will live and what they should communicate. References can define a direction, but the aim is never to reproduce somebody else's pictures.

details.title: Direction
details.text: Portrait, artist imagery, portfolio work, editorial or campaign can each require a different balance of clarity, atmosphere, context and observation. We define that balance together.

details.title: Individual production
details.text: Scope, location, styling, production costs, usage and delivery are discussed for the actual assignment. I do not work from a fixed package of images or looks.

workingFormats.lead: We work together because a photographic idea and my visual direction interest both of us.
workingFormats.description: A collaboration is an unpaid photographic project, not an unpaid commissioned portfolio session. It gives me room to develop my work together with a person who connects with that direction.

series.caption: A collaboration develops the photographic work for both sides without turning it into a client assignment.

details.title: Shared interest
details.text: Ideas are welcome, but the project is not built around a list of predetermined portfolio or social-media images. Both sides should connect with what we are trying to explore.

details.title: Unpaid, not cost-free
details.text: Neither side charges the other for the collaboration itself. Production costs may still arise for make-up, hair, styling, decoration, materials, travel or locations. If they do, we agree beforehand how they are shared.

details.title: Authorship and use
details.text: Selection, editing and sequencing of photographs published under my name remain part of my authorship. How both sides may use the material is discussed openly before the project.

workingFormats.quote: Both sides should leave the project with something meaningful — not necessarily the same thing.

about.title: A photographer, and a life outside photography.
paragraphs: I am Steffen Lauterbach, a semi-professional photographer living near Bern, Switzerland. I am the father of three adult daughters and, after graduating from university, spent most of my professional life working as an IT specialist.

Photography developed alongside that life and has become an increasingly important part of it. I have a particular affection for older photographic equipment, manual lenses and analogue cameras — not primarily from nostalgia, but because they encourage a slower and more deliberate way of seeing.

That way of looking also shapes my digital work. I am interested in people, but equally in the space around them and in the small relationships inside the frame that can turn a photograph into more than a picture of its subject.

series.caption: Digital and analogue approaches belong to the same way of seeing.

items.question: I need specific photographs. Is that a collaboration?
items.answer: If your requirements define the purpose and expected result, it is a commission. A free collaboration starts from a shared interest in a photographic project rather than from a client brief.

items.question: Can I apply for a free project?
items.answer: Yes. Send a current portfolio or a few recent photographs and tell me what connects you to my work. A collaboration makes sense when there is a strong fit with a current idea or direction.

items.question: Do you pay models?
items.answer: Sometimes. For my own independent photographic projects I may book and pay a professional model when a specific person is needed. This is separate from the two ways of working together described on this page.

items.question: Do I need professional modelling experience?
items.answer: No. Experience can be useful, but presence, openness, reliability and the ability to stay with a quiet situation can matter just as much.

items.question: What should I expect from a session?
items.answer: A calm and concentrated process rather than continuous shooting and constant changes. We may work with very small variations for a while when a situation has potential.

items.question: What about image use and publication?
items.answer: Usage depends on the type and purpose of the work and is agreed before the session. If a project requires specific limits, exclusivity or first-publication arrangements, those should be discussed before we confirm it.

studio.title: Bernapark
studio.description: My 103 m² studio is located in Bernapark, Deisswil near Bern. The high industrial space can be used with daylight or fully controlled studio light, and the surrounding area also gives us options outside the studio.
studio.contactText: Tell me briefly who you are, what you would like to create and whether you are enquiring about a commission or a creative collaboration.
studio.closing: If the direction feels right, we can start with a conversation.
